---
Sunlight appears white but is actually made up of all the colors of the visible spectrum. As sunlight passes through Earth's atmosphere, molecules and tiny particles scatter the shorter blue wavelengths of light far more than the longer red wavelengths, a phenomenon known as Rayleigh scattering. This scattered blue light reaches our eyes from all directions across the sky, which is why we perceive it as blue.
